matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and verify that the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you have a candidate transformed equation, before finalizing it, compute the numeric values and check that the left‑hand side equals the right‑hand side.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without confirming that the two sides are numerically equal.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A matchstick keeps its orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) when moved; you cannot rotate it to a different orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When deciding where to relocate a stick, ensure the destination expects a stick of the same orientation.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn a vertical stick from an ‘I’ into a diagonal part of an ‘X’.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick move may affect at most two distinct characters: the source character loses the stick and the destination character gains it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, identify the source and destination characters; no other characters may change.
matchstick.example: Changing three characters simultaneously, such as turning ‘VII’ into ‘X’ while also altering ‘VI’.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Only certain Roman‑numeral pairs can be changed by moving a single stick while keeping both characters valid (e.g., I ↔ II, V ↔ VI, X ↔ XV).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you consider moving a stick from one numeral to another, verify that the source numeral can lose that stick and still be a valid numeral, and that the destination numeral can gain it and become a valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical stick from ‘VI’ to make ‘V’, which is invalid because ‘V’ does not contain a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must be a single line beginning with the exact phrase ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the transformed equation, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When outputting the answer, ensure the line matches the required format exactly.
matchstick.example: Providing just the equation without the required prefix, or using lowercase letters.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’; removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a plus to a minus or vice versa, move a vertical stick accordingly.
matchstick.example: Turning a ‘+’ into an ‘=’ by moving a vertical stick (invalid conversion).

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: Removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ (turning it into ‘‑’) and adding that stick to a numeral that can accept a vertical stick (e.g., turning ‘V’ into ‘VI’ or adding an extra ‘I’) yields a valid transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to create an extra I in a numeral, consider taking the vertical stick from a plus sign.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to a numeral but forgetting to change the ‘+’ into ‘‑’, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Removing one horizontal line from ‘=’ turns it into ‘‑’; adding a horizontal line to ‘‑’ turns it into ‘=’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change an equals sign to a minus or vice versa, move a horizontal stick accordingly.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from ‘=’ but not adding it elsewhere, resulting in a missing stick.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals (I ↔ I)
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick (the I) from a numeral that contains an I character to another numeral that also contains an I character swaps the I’s while keeping both numerals valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to exchange an I between two numerals, e.g., turning ‘VII + VI’ into ‘VI + VII’.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to a V, which would produce an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Validate single-stick transformation feasibility
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, ensure that the source character can lose that stick and remain a valid Roman numeral or operator, and that the destination character can gain that stick (in the same orientation) and also become a valid Roman numeral or operator. This guarantees the move is possible with exactly one stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before committing to a proposed change, check both the source and destination characters against a list of known single‑stick transformations to confirm feasibility.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘VII’ to ‘X’ by moving a stick is invalid because no single‑stick removal from ‘VII’ yields a shape that can become ‘X’ while keeping both characters valid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on symbol manipulation without checking whether the resulting equation is numerically true.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert each Roman numeral to its integer value after a proposed transformation and verify that the equality holds before outputting.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may produce a character that does not correspond to any standard Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that both the source and destination characters remain valid Roman numerals or operators after the stick move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may remove or add sticks to an operator in a way that yields a non‑existent operator (e.g., turning ‘+’ into a lone vertical line).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only apply known operator conversions: ‘+’ ↔ ‘‑’ via vertical stick, ‘=’ ↔ ‘‑’ via horizontal stick.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a character without placing it on another, violating the rule that the stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick that is taken from a source must be added to a destination character; track both ends of the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs the transformed equation without the required prefix or with wrong casing/spacing.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Produce a single line that starts exactly with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the equation in uppercase, collapsing whitespace.
